item.title: One of the major problems of the antisemitism paradigm is that it converges with antizionism's own rhetorics of denial. By treating the classical antisemitism of 19th- and 20th-century Europe as the prototype and model of all 'antisemitism,' it reproduces the notion that antizionism is not 'real antisemitism' as long as it diverges from that model. The continued reliance on the single category of antisemitism—while refusing to name antizionism itself—continually reproduces this permission structure, one sustained both by Jewish discourse and by antizionists. It sustains a discourse of denial throughout society, even as a massive hate movement unfolds before everyone's eyes.
